purpose: Define which terms are globally shared, ontology-owned, surface-owned, contested, or forbidden to collapse before graph memory is consumed by DungeonMindBuddy surfaces.

shared_semantic_envelope.notes: The source object or artifact from which source anchors and units derive.
A stable locator to the source-backed unit or span.
The projection-safe source-backed unit returned to surfaces.
A citation/reference handle for source-backed claims and anchors.
Trace of how graph output is grounded.
Prevents display summaries or diagnostics from being treated as source evidence.
Indicates whether a record is canonical, candidate, diagnostic, generated, or otherwise authority-limited.
Preserves privacy and player/DM-facing visibility boundaries.
Prevents prep, rumor, generated candidate, diagnostic-only records, and played truth from collapsing into known fact.
A structured warning/error explaining why a graph-derived payload is blocked, degraded, or diagnostic-only.
A claim that must have source refs and an evidence role.
A display/navigation aid that may be shared as a field name but is never evidence.
A diagnostic-only record that cannot be shown as canon.

contested_terms.why_ambiguous: It can name source content, generated output, combat-local state, promoted corpus content, or a visible UI card.
contested_terms.graph_memory_meaning: May be a source artifact, generated candidate, combat-local acceptance, promoted corpus record, or indexed content.
contested_terms.surface_meaning: A visible statblock projection or workflow output.
contested_terms.boundary_rule: Keep statblock as a surface projection kind; require lifecycle/provenance/source refs for graph-derived statblock payloads.
contested_terms.detection: Report statblock-like payloads missing lifecycle, authority, evidence role, or source refs.

contested_terms.why_ambiguous: It can be a display convenience, a generated digest, or be mistaken for source evidence.
contested_terms.graph_memory_meaning: A derived display/navigation aid that is not evidence.
contested_terms.surface_meaning: Short prose shown in a drawer, chip preview, or planning card.
contested_terms.boundary_rule: Summaries may be displayed but must not be treated as source evidence.
contested_terms.detection: Flag summary text used with evidence_role=source_evidence without source refs.

contested_terms.why_ambiguous: It can refer to taxonomy relationships, corpus/source navigation, UI routes, or reference-resolution paths.
contested_terms.graph_memory_meaning: A taxonomy/relationship/navigation concept that may connect entities, source units, or corpus locations.
contested_terms.boundary_rule: Do not collapse graph route semantics and UI navigation routes; adapter may map between them explicitly.
contested_terms.detection: Report route payloads that lack source-family, relation type, or provenance.

contested_terms.why_ambiguous: It can mean corpus file, recap record, graph provenance, UI citation label, or user-entered content.
contested_terms.graph_memory_meaning: The artifact and provenance trail grounding a claim or candidate.
contested_terms.surface_meaning: A human-readable citation, drawer link, or origin label.
contested_terms.boundary_rule: Expose source labels only with source refs/anchors and provenance metadata.
contested_terms.detection: Flag source labels without source_ref or source_anchor.

contested_terms.why_ambiguous: It can be a stable source locator, a UI scroll target, or a reference chip target.
contested_terms.graph_memory_meaning: A stable locator to a source-backed unit or span.
contested_terms.surface_meaning: A navigation target or display affordance.
contested_terms.boundary_rule: UI anchors may point at source anchors, but must not redefine source-anchor stability.
contested_terms.detection: Flag graph-derived payloads with UI-only anchors and no source_anchor.

contested_terms.why_ambiguous: It can mean promoted campaign truth, displayed accepted content, or user-visible convenience.
contested_terms.graph_memory_meaning: An authority/lifecycle state backed by provenance and promotion rules.
contested_terms.surface_meaning: A label implying content is official, accepted, or safe to use.
contested_terms.boundary_rule: Canon labels require authority_state and lifecycle_state that explicitly permit them.
contested_terms.detection: Flag canon display without authority_state, lifecycle_state, and provenance.

contested_terms.why_ambiguous: It can be writer workflow state, generated candidate state, or UI edit state.
contested_terms.boundary_rule: Draft UI state must not imply graph candidate promotion or demotion.
contested_terms.detection: Flag draft records with promoted/canonical authority unless provenance explains promotion.

contested_terms.why_ambiguous: It can mean combat-local acceptance, user confirmation, promoted corpus truth, or validation acceptance.
contested_terms.graph_memory_meaning: A lifecycle transition whose scope must be explicit.
contested_terms.surface_meaning: A workflow action or local display state.
contested_terms.boundary_rule: Accepted must state scope: combat-local, session-local, corpus-promoted, or diagnostic.
contested_terms.detection: Flag accepted payloads missing lifecycle_state and promotion_state/scope.

contested_terms.why_ambiguous: It can mean LLM output, deterministic projection, materialized graph record, or user-generated note.
contested_terms.graph_memory_meaning: A provenance fact requiring generator/source distinction and authority limits.
contested_terms.surface_meaning: Tool output ready for review or display.
contested_terms.boundary_rule: Generated content remains authority-limited until source/provenance/lifecycle permit promotion.
contested_terms.detection: Flag generated claims shown as source-backed evidence without source refs.

contested_terms.why_ambiguous: It can mean taxonomy promotion, corpus writeback, UI accept action, or candidate validation.
contested_terms.graph_memory_meaning: A governed transition into a higher authority or lifecycle state.
contested_terms.surface_meaning: An affordance or workflow completion step.
contested_terms.boundary_rule: Promotion must remain ontology-owned and auditable; UI actions may request but not redefine it.
contested_terms.detection: Flag promotion-like actions without promotion_state and provenance.

contested_terms.why_ambiguous: It can mean retrieval index, corpus table of contents, UI list, or source ordering.
contested_terms.graph_memory_meaning: A derived navigation/retrieval structure with provenance and scope.
contested_terms.surface_meaning: A list, lookup, or drawer section organization.
contested_terms.boundary_rule: Indexes are not evidence; indexed content still needs source refs and evidence roles.
contested_terms.detection: Flag indexed summaries treated as source evidence.

forbidden_collapses.description: Display summaries must not be treated as source evidence.
Generated candidates, rumors, prep, diagnostic-only records, and played truth must not collapse into a generic known-fact state.
Surface ref types such as npc, location, statblock, and roll-table must not become ontology ownership.
Projection payloads must not be treated as promoted corpus truth unless lifecycle/provenance says so.
